en: And that through a very fast network and through new protocols like NVMe over Fabrics and through new media types that allow us to save not just data on the other side of the network, but also metadata, we were able to have all of the nodes see all of the information as if it was directly attached.
zh: 通过一个非常快的网络、通过像 NVMe over Fabrics 这样的新协议、以及通过新的介质类型——它们让我们不仅能把数据存储在网络的另一端，还能存储元数据——我们得以让所有节点都能看到所有信息，就好像它们是直接连接的一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's what led us to being able to do what we call shared everything.
zh: 这就是我们所说的「共享一切」（shared everything）的由来。

speaker: Unknown
en: All of the nodes now don't need to communicate with each other because they share access to all of the information.
zh: 现在所有节点不需要互相通信，因为它们共享对所有信息的访问。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's the basic idea behind our architecture.
zh: 这就是我们架构背后的基本理念。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it proved really, really good for a new type of storage system for AI, and then for a new type of database for AI, and then for a new way to orchestrate compute for AI.
zh: 而事实证明，它对于一种新型 AI 存储系统非常非常好，然后对于一种新型 AI 数据库也非常好，接着对于一种编排 AI 计算的新方式也非常好。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we realized over the years, our customers forced us to realize that it's not just storage that needs to be redone, but the entire part of that stack that needs to be redone.
zh: 这些年来我们意识到——是我们的客户迫使我们意识到——不只是存储需要重做，而是那一整层技术栈都需要重做。

speaker: Unknown
en: As an aside, I'm smiling.
zh: 顺便说一句，我在笑。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so, thank you.
zh: 所以，谢谢你们。

en: Is that part of why that middle layer is less known?
zh: 这是不是中间这一层不那么知名的部分原因？

en: There aren't.

en: The ones that we're competing with started...

zh: 比我们早三年，或者早三十年。

en: And so that's our advantage today.
zh: 所以这就是我们今天的优势。

en: That's our moat, the fact that we're the only ones with this architecture.

en: And it's true that there aren't many other companies in our layer, I think mainly because it's not sexy.
zh: 确实，我们这一层的公司不多，我认为主要是因为它不性感。

zh: 建一家模型公司或应用公司，比建那些管道工程要有吸引力得多。

en: And the days architecture is still at the very basis of what you do, all products currently.
zh: 而 Weka 的架构仍然是你们所做一切的最底层基础，目前所有产品都是。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's right.
zh: 没错。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have one product that's this operating system, but all of the parts that we're adding are based on days.
zh: 我们有一个产品，就是这个操作系统，但我们正在添加的所有部件都基于 Weka。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's part of the reason why we can't take open source and bolt it on top.
zh: 这也是为什么我们不能拿开源来直接装在上面的部分原因。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have to write most of it ourselves.
zh: 我们必须自己编写大部分东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why did you start building databases on top?
zh: 你们为什么开始在存储之上构建数据库？

speaker: Unknown
en: What was not addressed by the market that you needed to build?
zh: 市场上有什么是你需要自己构建而没有被解决的？

speaker: Unknown
en: Same as with storage.
zh: 和存储一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: We realized that there was a trade-off between price and performance and scale and resilience and ease of use in the world of database in the same way that there was in the world of storage.
zh: 我们意识到，在数据库领域同样存在价格、性能、规模、韧性和易用性之间的取舍，就像存储领域一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: We realized that because our customers told us that.
zh: 我们意识到这一点，是因为我们的客户告诉我们的。

zh: 新加坡，他们有大量的摄像头画面接入，所有这些画面都需要在图像进入时被向量化，这导致了数万亿的向量需要放进一个数据库。

speaker: Unknown
en: There isn't a database that was built for trillions of rows.
zh: 目前还没有为万亿行数据而构建的数据库。

speaker: Unknown

zh: 还没有为数千个智能体同时分析系统中正在发生的不同方面而构建的数据库。

speaker: Unknown
en: Old stack databases were built for big amounts of data, which today seem very, very small.
zh: 旧技术栈的数据库是为大量数据而构建的,而这些数据量在今天看来非常非常小。

speaker: Unknown
en: They were built for people running queries and doing the analysis.
zh: 它们是为人们运行查询和做分析而构建的。

speaker: Unknown

zh: 再说一次,

speaker: Unknown

zh: 那种旧架构,无共享架构,其可扩展性不足以达到我们今天需要的水平。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's scale, right?
zh: 所以这是规模问题,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, just to...
zh: 我是说,只是……

en: I'll push back a little bit or probe, you know, I'm sure like Databricks or like Snowflake would say, well, no, no, no, we massively scalable and we can just run massive analytics on data and including some in real time with newer products.
zh: 我会稍微反驳或追问一下,你知道,我确信像 Databricks 或 Snowflake 会说,不,不,不,我们可以大规模扩展,可以对数据运行大规模分析,包括用新产品做一些实时分析。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then, you know, I think...
zh: 然后,你知道,我想……

speaker: Unknown
en: Some people would say, well, storage was solved, like that's S3, that's infinitely scalable.
zh: 有些人会说,存储已经被解决了,比如那就是 S3,那是无限可扩展的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But what we're saying here is that all of this may be true for certain use cases, but not for what we're talking about here.
zh: 但我们在这里说的是,所有这些对某些用例可能成立,但对我们这里谈论的不成立。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think both of those companies that you mentioned started again about five years before us.
zh: 我记得你提到的那两家公司都比我们早成立大约五年。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so they too are built on that older architecture and they started top down.
zh: 所以它们同样建立在那种较旧的架构之上,而且它们是自上而下起步的。

speaker: Unknown
en: They are based on underlying cloud services like S3, which were not built for this era of AI.
zh: 它们基于像 S3 这样的底层云服务,而这些服务并不是为这个 AI 时代而构建的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we're seeing that today.
zh: 我们今天正在看到这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's a big part of the reason these AI clouds are starting to pop up because the traditional hyperscalers that built S3 built the old stack and these new AI clouds are building the new stack and now the older clouds need to adapt in order to stay relevant.
zh: 这是这些 AI 云开始涌现的一大原因,因为构建了 S3 的传统超大规模云厂商构建的是旧技术栈,而这些新的 AI 云正在构建新技术栈,现在较旧的云需要调整以保持相关性。

speaker: Unknown
en: So is the ask to customer as they build those AI factories to basically move all the data to VAST?
zh: 那么,在客户构建这些 AI 工厂时,是要他们基本上把所有数据迁移到 VAST 吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: They don't have to start by moving all the data to VAST.
zh: 他们不必一开始就把所有数据迁移到 VAST。

speaker: Unknown
en: Usually we start by just serving the new applications, just serving the new AI applications.
zh: 通常我们只是先服务新应用,只服务新的 AI 应用。

speaker: Unknown
en: Usually what happens after that is that
zh: 通常在那之后发生的是

speaker: Unknown
en: The customer, the enterprise, the organization realize that this is actually useful and I want it to access the entirety of my dataset rather than just this subset.
zh: 客户、企业、组织意识到这确实有用,我希望它访问我的整个数据集,而不仅仅是这个子集。

speaker: Unknown
en: The good news is that we support all of the old stack interfaces.
zh: 好消息是,我们支持所有旧技术栈的接口。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so if you're talking storage, S3, we support file systems, we support block devices, we support if you're talking databases, we support SQL.
zh: 所以如果说的是存储,有 S3,我们支持文件系统,我们支持块设备,如果说的是数据库,我们支持 SQL。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you're talking streaming, we support Kafka.
zh: 如果说的是流处理,我们支持 Kafka。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so it's very easy to plug in those old stack applications onto our platform in parallel to the new agentic workloads and AI applications.
zh: 因此,把这些旧技术栈的应用接入我们的平台非常容易,可以与新的智能体工作负载和 AI 应用并行运行。

speaker: Unknown
en: And in that sense, we become a bridge between the old world and the new world as companies.
zh: 从这个意义上说,当公司

speaker: Unknown
en: Make that journey.
zh: 踏上这段旅程时,我们成为旧世界与新世界之间的桥梁。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the end of the journey is that the old world merges into the new world.
zh: 但旅程的终点是旧世界融入新世界。

speaker: Unknown
en: Of course.
zh: 当然。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So obviously data gravity is a wonderful thing if you're vast.
zh: 显然,如果你是 VAST,数据引力是一件美妙的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do customers feel about the idea of like moving all the data ultimately to one vendor?
zh: 客户对最终把所有数据迁移到单一厂商这个想法感觉如何?

speaker: Unknown
en: So because the interfaces are all standard, it's just as easy for them to move off of us as it is to move onto us.
zh: 因为接口都是标准的,他们从我们这里迁走的容易程度和迁入我们这里的容易程度是一样的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's our job to make sure that they're happy.
zh: 确保他们满意是我们的工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: The one chart that I look at every morning is our customer happiness chart.
zh: 我每天早上看的唯一一张图表是我们的客户满意度图表。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's the only thing we care about.
zh: 这是我们唯一在乎的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: What does that look like?
zh: 那是什么样子的?

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you measure customer happiness?
zh: 你们如何衡量客户满意度?

speaker: Unknown
en: It has three colors.
zh: 它有三种颜色。

speaker: Unknown
en: It has green, it has yellow, it has red.
zh: 有绿色,有黄色,有红色。

speaker: Unknown
en: And anybody in the company is allowed to move a customer from green to yellow or from yellow to red.
zh: 公司里任何人都可以把一个客户从绿色移到黄色,或从黄色移到红色。

speaker: Unknown
en: But very few people are allowed to move them back.
zh: 但只有极少数人可以把它移回去。

speaker: Unknown
en: Based on what metrics?
zh: 基于什么指标?

speaker: Unknown
en: The only metric that really matters in order for us to move a customer back is that they say so.
zh: 要把一个客户移回去,唯一真正重要的指标是他们自己这么说。

speaker: Unknown
en: That they say we're happy now.
zh: 就是他们说我们现在满意了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Everything is good.
zh: 一切都好。

speaker: Unknown
en: Everything is solved.
zh: 一切都解决了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And yeah, that's what we work so hard every day to accomplish.
zh: 是的,这就是我们每天如此努力工作要实现的目标。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the numbers show that it's working.
zh: 我认为数据表明这是有效的。

speaker: Unknown
en: The numbers that people like you usually care about are net dollar retention, gross dollar retention.
zh: 像你这样的人通常关心的数字是净金额留存率、总金额留存率。

speaker: Unknown
en: We don't have any churn in the company, our gross dollar retention.
zh: 我们公司没有任何流失,我们的总金额留存率——

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not a hundred percent because a few of our customers have gone out of business over the years, but no one's actively decided I'm going to stop using Vast.
zh: 不是百分之百,因为这些年有少数客户倒闭了,但没有任何人是主动决定「我要停止使用 Vast」的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Which is something I'm very proud of.
zh: 这是我非常自豪的一件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: And on average, our customers double and triple the amount of data that they place on our systems every year.
zh: 平均而言,我们的客户每年放在我们系统里的数据量会翻倍甚至 triple。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's get into some of the technicality of how the data interacts with models.
zh: 我们来聊一些数据与模型交互的技术细节。

speaker: Unknown
en: What does it actually mean to move data to the GPU?
zh: 把数据移动到 GPU 到底意味着什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: And is it different for training compared to inference?
zh: 训练和推理在这方面有区别吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: Training is super simple.
zh: 训练超级简单。

speaker: Unknown
en: Training, you just need a lot of GPUs and you need to feed them with a lot of training data.
zh: 训练,你只需要大量 GPU,并且要给它们喂大量训练数据。

speaker: Unknown
en: Once in a while, they put down a checkpoint so that if something crashes, they don't have to go all the way back to the beginning.
zh: 每隔一段时间,它们会保存一个 checkpoint,这样如果崩溃了,就不用从头开始。

speaker: Unknown
en: But other than that, there's not much to it.
zh: 但除此之外,没有太多别的了。

speaker: Unknown
en: You need large scale.
zh: 你需要大规模。

speaker: Unknown
en: You need fast access.
zh: 你需要快速访问。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's it.
zh: 就这样。

speaker: Unknown
en: Inference is becoming a whole complex world of its own.
zh: 推理正在变成一个自身非常复杂的世界。

speaker: Unknown
en: Inference started by obviously requiring low latency access because people are on the other end prompting and they want fast responses.
zh: 推理一开始显然就需要低延迟访问,因为另一端有人在输入 prompt,他们想要快速响应。

speaker: Unknown
en: That meant that you need a distributed system close to where those people are at the edge.
zh: 那意味着你需要一个靠近那些人所在的边缘的分布式系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: That also means that you need a system that's always up.
zh: 那也意味着你需要一个永远在线的系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: Somebody once told me, one of the big model builders, that if
zh: 曾经有人——一个大模型制造商——告诉我,如果

speaker: Unknown
en: Training is down, nobody notices.
zh: 训练挂了,没人会注意到。

speaker: Unknown
en: If inference is down, there is no service.
zh: 如果推理挂了,就没有服务了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so it needs to be up 100% of the time.
zh: 所以它需要 100% 的时间都在线。

speaker: Unknown
en: Resilience, distributed nature, low latency, very secure environments, all of that is important in inference versus training.
zh: 韧性、分布式特性、低延迟、非常安全的环境,这些在推理侧都比训练侧更重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: But that's just the ground level.
zh: 但这只是最基础层面。

speaker: Unknown
en: Once we start talking about multiple models, once we start talking about agents, once we start talking about reinforced learning, definitely once we expand outside of the world of data centers into physical AI and actual devices, each one of those adds another layer that means that we need to develop a new set of tools.
zh: 一旦我们开始谈论多个模型,一旦我们开始谈论智能体,一旦我们开始谈论强化学习,尤其是一旦我们扩展到数据中心之外的世界,进入物理 AI 和实际设备,每一样都会增加一层,意味着我们需要开发一套新的工具。

speaker: Unknown
en: For example,
zh: 举例来说,

speaker: Unknown
en: Now that we have multiple models, each model is good at different things.
zh: 现在我们有多个模型,每个模型擅长不同的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I want to make sure that this prompt makes its way to that model because it's good at software development.
zh: 所以我想确保这个 prompt 能到达那个模型,因为它擅长软件开发。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want to make sure that this prompt makes its way to that model because it's inexpensive and this isn't a high value task.
zh: 我想确保这个 prompt 能到达那个模型,因为它便宜,而这不是一个高价值任务。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want to make sure that no sensitive information is exposed to this model because they're going to use that information for things that I don't want them to.
zh: 我想确保没有敏感信息暴露给这个模型,因为他们会用那些信息做我不希望他们做的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: Whereas here I have a contract that protects me.
zh: 而这里我有一份合同保护我。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so just that aspect of it is starting to get complex.
zh: 所以仅仅是这一个方面就开始变复杂了。

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: Context is just the last few minutes of conversation.
zh: 上下文就是最近几分钟的对话。

speaker: Unknown
en: We need short-term memory the last few weeks or long-term memory what happened two years ago to also be accessible through things like RAG into these environments.
zh: 我们还需要短期记忆(最近几周)或长期记忆(两年前发生了什么)也能通过 RAG 之类的机制在这些环境中被访问。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so all of that requires us to manage
zh: 所以这一切都需要我们管理

speaker: Unknown
en: Data, the raw data, the generated data, the input data, the weights of the model, the context.
zh: 数据、原始数据、生成的数据、输入数据、模型的权重、上下文。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we need to make sure that nobody sees information that they're not allowed to.

speaker: Unknown

zh: 尽管如此，没有任何排他性。

speaker: Unknown
en: We work with AMD, we work with other companies in parallel to working with NVIDIA.

speaker: Unknown

zh: 我们永远不能成为他们进步和取得成功路上的限制因素。

en: So we can't get into a mode where we're congratulating ourselves too much.
zh: 所以我们不能陷入过度自我祝贺的状态。

speaker: Unknown
en: We always have to be in this mode of somebody's going to kill us.
zh: 我们必须始终处于这种“总有人要干掉我们”的心态。

speaker: Unknown

en: So I think in the next 10 years we'll see more difference than we did in the last thousand years if this plays out in the way that it seems to be playing out.
zh: 所以我认为，如果事情按照它目前看来的方向发展，未来十年我们将看到比过去一千年更大的变化。

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown

zh: 我们需要确保它不会杀死我们，因此它是安全的，并且在这一路上我们设置好护栏，使我们作为人类能够
